subproblem.title: Monotonicity on B̄_{2r}(z) and finite mass of B_{2r}(z) give M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ Γρⁿ uniformly near B̄_r(z) (preliminary P8, the mass hypothesis of (IBL))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P), T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), z ∈ ℝ^P and r, Λ ∈ ℝ with r > 0 and Λ ≥ 0. Assume: (a) for all y ∈ ℝ^P and R ∈ ℝ with B̄_R(y) ⊆ B̄_{2r}(z), the function ρ ↦ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(y)}(T) (values in [0, ∞]) is monotone on the open interval (0, R); (b) M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T) ≠ ∞. Then there are δ > 0 and Γ ∈ ℝ such that M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γ·ρⁿ) for every b ∈ B̄_r(z), every x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and every ρ with 0 < ρ < δ. Here M_W(T) = T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞] is Simon's local mass, ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, B_ρ(y) is the open and B̄_R(y) the closed ball.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (z : Euclid P) (r Λ : ℝ), 0 < r → 0 ≤ Λ → (∀ (y : Euclid P) (R : ℝ), closedBall y R ⊆ closedBall z (2 * r) → MonotoneOn (fun ρ : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal (Real.exp (Λ * ρ) / ρ ^ n) * T.massOn (ball y ρ)) (Ioo 0 R)) → T.massOn (ball z (2 * r)) ≠ ∞ → ∃ δ Γ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ b ∈ closedBall z r, ∀ x' ∈ ball b δ, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → T.massOn (ball x' ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (Γ * ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: preliminary P8 of the parent's supplied proof (the mass hypothesis of (IBL) at a point b ∈ B̄_r(z)). There, (MON)(i) on the compact set K = B̄_{2r}(z) ⊆ U supplies the monotonicity (a), and P1 ((IM)(a) and the local integrability of the multiplicity of RT) supplies the finiteness (b). In this child (a) and (b) are hypotheses. The comparison M_{B_{r/4}(x′)}(T) ≤ M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T), which P8 obtains from the weight μ_T, is obtained here from the monotonicity of the local mass in the set: M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal(T(ω)) over test forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W and Euclidean covector norm (covectorEuclideanNorm) ≤ 1 at every point, so W₁ ⊆ W₂ implies M_{W₁}(T) ≤ M_{W₂}(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono, SimonGMT Chapter06/Mass.lean).
1. (Constants.) Put Γ′ := ofReal(e^{Λ·(r/4)}/(r/4)ⁿ)·M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T) ∈ [0, ∞]. Since ofReal(·) ≠ ∞ and M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T) ≠ ∞ by (b), Γ′ ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top). Put δ := r/4 > 0 and Γ := Γ′.toReal ≥ 0. Note that δ and Γ do not depend on b.
2. (Geometry.) Let b ∈ B̄_r(z), x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and 0 < ρ < δ. Then dist(x′, z) ≤ dist(x′, b) + dist(b, z) < r/4 + r = 5r/4. Consequently:
 (i) B̄_{r/2}(x′) ⊆ B̄_{2r}(z): if dist(w, x′) ≤ r/2 then dist(w, z) ≤ dist(w, x′) + dist(x′, z) < r/2 + 5r/4 = 7r/4 ≤ 2r;
 (ii) B_{r/4}(x′) ⊆ B_{2r}(z): if dist(w, x′) < r/4 then dist(w, z) < r/4 + 5r/4 = 3r/2 < 2r.
3. (Monotonicity.) By (i), hypothesis (a) applies with (y, R) := (x′, r/2): the function f(τ) := ofReal(e^{Λτ}/τⁿ)·M_{B_τ(x′)}(T) is monotone on (0, r/2). Both ρ and r/4 lie in (0, r/2), and ρ ≤ r/4 (indeed ρ < δ = r/4). Hence f(ρ) ≤ f(r/4).
4. (Bound at radius r/4.) By (ii) and the monotonicity of the local mass in the set, M_{B_{r/4}(x′)}(T) ≤ M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T). Multiplying by ofReal(e^{Λ(r/4)}/(r/4)ⁿ) gives f(r/4) ≤ Γ′.
5. (Removing the exponential.) Since Λ ≥ 0 and ρ > 0 we have Λρ ≥ 0, so e^{Λρ} ≥ 1 (Real.one_le_exp). Dividing by ρⁿ > 0 gives 1/ρⁿ ≤ e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ, hence ofReal(1/ρⁿ) ≤ ofReal(e^{Λρ}/ρⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal), and therefore ofReal(1/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ f(ρ) ≤ f(r/4) ≤ Γ′ by steps 3 and 4.
6. (Conclusion.) Since ρⁿ > 0, ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal(1/ρⁿ) = ofReal(ρⁿ·(1/ρⁿ)) = ofReal(1) = 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Hence
 M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) = ofReal(ρⁿ)·(ofReal(1/ρⁿ)·M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T)) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·Γ′ (step 5).
 As Γ′ ≠ ∞, Γ′ = ofReal(Γ′.toReal) = ofReal(Γ) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal), so ofReal(ρⁿ)·Γ′ = ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal(Γ) = ofReal(Γ·ρⁿ) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ρⁿ ≥ 0).
 Thus M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all b ∈ B̄_r(z), x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and 0 < ρ < δ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take δ := r/4 and Γ := (ofReal(e^{Λr/4}/(r/4)ⁿ)·M_{B_{2r}(z)}(T)).toReal, finite by (b).
For b ∈ B̄_r(z) and x′ ∈ B_{r/4}(b): dist(x′, z) < 5r/4, so B̄_{r/2}(x′) ⊆ B̄_{2r}(z) and B_{r/4}(x′) ⊆ B_{2r}(z).
Monotonicity on (0, r/2) gives f(ρ) ≤ f(r/4), and f(r/4) ≤ Γ′ because the local mass is monotone in the set.
e^{Λρ} ≥ 1 removes the exponential; multiplying by ofReal(ρⁿ) gives M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(ρⁿ)·Γ′ = ofReal(Γρⁿ).

audit.reason: All hypotheses match the type. The constants δ = r/4 and Γ are independent of b; the ball inclusions justify monotonicity and mass comparison. Finiteness and positive ENNReal factors justify the final cancellation, including n = 0. The proof is complete and the name is unreserved.

subproblem.title: Along blow-ups with mass-measure convergence, the rescaled IMRep weights converge vaguely to the weight of the limit (preliminary P7 with MassMeasuresConverge)
subproblem.statement: Assume (BUI) — verbatim the frozen type of the registered dependency blowup_imrep of the grandparent node blowup_class (the reused accepted rep_pushforward): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ ℝ^P, λ > 0 and every IMRep R of T in U there is an IMRep R′ in dilation x λ '' U representing blowUp T x λ with R′.measure(s) = ofReal(λ⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure((dilation x λ)⁻¹(s)) for every Borel s. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P, A ∈ 𝒟_n(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V n) with an IMRep R of A in V (R.Represents A), a ∈ ℝ^P, scales s_j > 0 (j ∈ ℕ), and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with an IMRep R_C of C in ℝ^P. Suppose MassMeasuresConverge (j ↦ blowUp A a s_j) C. Then for every continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support, ∫ f d(ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map(dilation a s_j)) → ∫ f dR_C.measure as j → ∞, where dilation a s (v) = s⁻¹(v − a).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (x : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → ∃ R' : IMRep (dilation x lam '' U) n, R'.Represents (blowUp T x lam hlam.ne') ∧ ∀ s : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet s → R'.measure s = ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ n) * R.measure (dilation x lam ⁻¹' s)) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (A : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (R : IMRep V n) (a : Euclid P) (ss : ℕ → ℝ) (hss : ∀ j, 0 < ss j) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (RC : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), R.Represents A → RC.Represents C → MassMeasuresConverge (fun j => blowUp A a (ss j) (hss j).ne') C → ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, f x ∂(ENNReal.ofReal ((ss j)⁻¹ ^ n) • R.measure.map (dilation a (ss j)))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂RC.measure))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: preliminary P7 (IMReps of blow-ups and their weights) of the parent's supplied proof, together with the use of MassMeasuresConverge in the convergence steps of cases (PS-i) (A := T, R := RT, a := p, s_j := tλ_{φ(j)}) and (ZS-i) (A := S, R := RS, a := y, s_j := λ_{φ(j)}).
Notation: η_j := dilation a s_j, so η_j(v) = −(s_j⁻¹•a) + s_j⁻¹•v = s_j⁻¹(v − a); m_j := ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map η_j.
1. (Measurability of the dilations.) For every s ∈ ℝ, dilation a s is v ↦ −(s⁻¹•a) + dilationCLM P s v, the sum of a constant and a continuous linear map. Hence it is continuous and therefore Borel measurable.
2. (IMReps of the blow-ups.) For each j, apply (BUI) to (P, n, V, A, a, s_j > 0, R), using R.Represents A. It gives an IMRep R_j in dilation a s_j '' V with R_j.Represents (blowUp A a s_j) and R_j.measure(B) = ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure(η_j⁻¹(B)) for every Borel set B. Choose one such R_j for every j ∈ ℕ (axiom of choice).
3. (Their weights are the rescaled measures.) Let j ∈ ℕ and let B be Borel. By the definition of the scalar multiple of a measure and of the push-forward (Measure.smul_apply; Measure.map_apply, which applies because η_j is measurable by step 1 and B is Borel),
 m_j(B) = ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ)·(R.measure.map η_j)(B) = ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure(η_j⁻¹(B)) = R_j.measure(B) (step 2).
 Measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext), so R_j.measure = m_j for every j.
4. (Mass-measure convergence.) By definition, MassMeasuresConverge (j ↦ blowUp A a s_j) C says: for every family of IMReps of the blow-ups (one in each domain dilation a s_j '' V), every IMRep of C in ℝ^P and every continuous compactly supported f with tsupport f ⊆ ℝ^P, the integrals of f against the weights converge. Apply it to the family (R_j) of step 2, to R_C, to f and to tsupport f ⊆ ℝ^P = univ. This gives ∫ f dR_j.measure → ∫ f dR_C.measure as j → ∞.
5. (Conclusion.) By step 3, ∫ f dR_j.measure = ∫ f dm_j for every j. Hence ∫ f d(ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map(dilation a s_j)) → ∫ f dR_C.measure. ∎
proof_key_steps: dilation a s is an affine map with continuous linear part, hence continuous and measurable.
(BUI) gives, for every j, an IMRep R_j of blowUp A a s_j whose weight is B ↦ ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ)·R.measure((dilation a s_j)⁻¹(B)); choose them for all j.
Measure.ext with Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply: R_j.measure = ofReal(s_j⁻¹ⁿ) • R.measure.map(dilation a s_j).
MassMeasuresConverge applied to (R_j), R_C, f and tsupport f ⊆ univ gives the convergence of ∫ f dR_j.measure = ∫ f d(rescaled weight) to ∫ f dR_C.measure.

audit.reason: BUI is copied verbatim as a hypothesis. The proof constructs representations on the correct varying domains, identifies their weights using measurable dilations and Measure.ext, and applies the exact definition of MassMeasuresConverge. subproblem.title: The zero current in ℝ^P is represented by the empty IMRep, whose weight is the zero measure (preliminary P4)
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there is an integer multiplicity representation R of the zero current of ℝ^P: an IMRep R in univ ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P (IMRep univ n) with R.Represents (0 : GeometricCurrentOn univ n), i.e. 0(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_{R.carrier} R.mult·⟨ω, R.orient⟩ dHⁿ for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), and whose weight R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞R.carrier).withDensity R.mult is the zero measure. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R.Represents (0 : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) ∧ R.measure = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: preliminary P4 ('the zero member') of the parent's supplied proof, used there in cases (PS-ii) and (ZS-ii) to show 0 ∈ 𝓜. Simon treats the zero current as the integer multiplicity current τ(∅, θ, ξ) (Ch. 6, 3.1).
Notation: Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P = Euclid P.
1. (The triple.) Let R_∅ have carrier ∅, multiplicity θ :≡ 0 and orientation ξ :≡ 0 (the zero n-vector). We check the fields of IMRep univ n.
 (a) ∅ is a Borel set (MeasurableSet.empty) and ∅ ⊆ univ.
 (b) ∅ is countably n-rectifiable: Hⁿ(∅) = 0 (measure_empty), and every Hⁿ-null set is countably n-rectifiable (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero: the null set itself is the exceptional set M₀ of Definition 1.1).
 (c) θ is constant, hence measurable. The positivity condition 'θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ ∅' is vacuous.
 (d) For every compact K ⊆ univ, ∅ ∩ K = ∅ and Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 (Measure.restrict_empty), so ∫⁻_{∅∩K} θ dHⁿ = ∫⁻ θ d0 = 0 ≠ ∞ (lintegral_zero_measure).
 (e) ξ is constant, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞∅ (aestronglyMeasurable_const).
 (f) The orientation condition is required only Hⁿ⌞∅-almost everywhere. Since Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0, its almost-everywhere filter is ⊥ (ae_zero), so every property, in particular this one, holds a.e.
 Hence R_∅ is an IMRep in univ.
2. (R_∅ represents 0.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) be a test form. By definition R_∅.action ω = ∫_{x∈∅} θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ = ∫ … d(Hⁿ⌞∅) = ∫ … d0 = 0 (Measure.restrict_empty, integral_zero_measure). The zero current satisfies 0(ω) = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply). Hence 0(ω) = R_∅.action ω for every ω, i.e. R_∅.Represents 0.
3. (Zero weight.) R_∅.measure = (Hⁿ⌞∅).withDensity θ = (0 : Measure).withDensity θ. For every Borel set s, withDensity_apply gives (0).withDensity θ (s) = ∫⁻_s θ d0 = 0 = 0(s). Two measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal (Measure.ext), so R_∅.measure = 0.
Steps 1–3 show that R := R_∅ has the required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0; every IMRep field holds because Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 (rectifiability by countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, a.e. conditions by ae_zero).
Its action is an integral against the zero measure, so it equals 0 = 0(ω); hence it represents the zero current of ℝ^P.
Its weight is a density against the zero measure, so R.measure = 0 (Measure.ext with withDensity_apply).

subproblem.title: Iterated blow-ups of a zero-scale limit at a point of the unit ball are again zero-scale limits of blow-ups of T (the (IBL) membership step)
subproblem.statement: Assume (IBL) — verbatim the frozen type of the registered dependency iterated_blowup_limit of the grandparent node blowup_class: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U), x ∈ U, x_i → x, λ_i > 0 with λ_i → 0, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), y ∈ ℝ^P, s_k > 0 with s_k → 0 and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P): if there are δ > 0 and Γ with M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all x′ ∈ B_δ(x) and 0 < ρ < δ, blowUp T x_i λ_i ⇀ S and blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C (ConvergesWeakly), then there is a strictly increasing φ with blowUp T (x_{φ(k)} + λ_{φ(k)}•y) (λ_{φ(k)}s_k) ⇀ C. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), z ∈ ℝ^P, r ∈ ℝ, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), points c_i ∈ ℝ^P and scales t_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ), and b ∈ U, such that dist(c_i, z) < r − t_i for every i, t_i → 0, c_i → b, blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S in ℝ^P (ConvergesWeakly), and there are δ > 0 and Γ ∈ ℝ with M_{B_ρ(x′)}(T) ≤ ofReal(Γρⁿ) for all x′ ∈ B_δ(b) and 0 < ρ < δ. Let y ∈ ℝ^P with ‖y‖ < 1, s_k > 0 (k ∈ ℕ) with s_k → 0, and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C. Then there are points c′_k ∈ ℝ^P and scales t′_k > 0 (k ∈ ℕ) such that dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k for every k, t′_k → 0, c′_k → b and blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the class-membership step 'ν ∈ 𝓜' of cases (ZS-i) and (ZS-ii) of the parent's supplied proof (Simon 7.3.3, proof of (1), chapter-07.txt lines 443–486: a tangent cone of a member of 𝒯₀ is again in 𝒯₀ because η_{y,s#}η_{x_i,λ_i#}T = η_{x_i+λ_iy, λ_is#}T). Here C is arbitrary; in the parent C is a tangent cone of S at y, or the zero current.
1. (Iterated limit.) Apply (IBL) with P, n, U (open), T, x := b ∈ U, xs := (c_i), lams := (t_i) (positive), S, y, ss := (s_k) (positive) and C. Its hypotheses are exactly the assumptions: c_i → b, t_i → 0, s_k → 0, the mass bound at b with (δ, Γ), blowUp T c_i t_i ⇀ S and blowUp S y s_k ⇀ C. It gives a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with blowUp T (c_{φ(k)} + t_{φ(k)}•y) (t_{φ(k)}s_k) ⇀ C.
2. (A tail with small scales.) Since ‖y‖ < 1, the number 1 − ‖y‖ is positive, so {s ∈ ℝ : s < 1 − ‖y‖} is a neighbourhood of 0. As s_k → 0, there is k₀ ∈ ℕ with s_k < 1 − ‖y‖ for all k ≥ k₀.
3. (New data.) For k ∈ ℕ put i(k) := φ(k + k₀), c′_k := c_{i(k)} + t_{i(k)}•y and t′_k := t_{i(k)}·s_{k+k₀}. Then t′_k > 0 as a product of two positive numbers.
4. (The admissibility inequality.) Fix k. Since t_{i(k)} > 0, dist(c′_k, c_{i(k)}) = ‖t_{i(k)}•y‖ = t_{i(k)}‖y‖. By the triangle inequality and the assumption dist(c_{i(k)}, z) < r − t_{i(k)},
 dist(c′_k, z) ≤ dist(c′_k, c_{i(k)}) + dist(c_{i(k)}, z) < t_{i(k)}‖y‖ + r − t_{i(k)} = r − t_{i(k)}(1 − ‖y‖).
 Since k + k₀ ≥ k₀, step 2 gives s_{k+k₀} < 1 − ‖y‖, so t_{i(k)}(1 − ‖y‖) > t_{i(k)}s_{k+k₀} = t′_k (t_{i(k)} > 0). Hence dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k.
5. (Limits of the data.) The map k ↦ k + k₀ tends to ∞ (tendsto_add_atTop_nat), and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ tends to ∞ (StrictMono.tendsto_atTop); hence i(k) → ∞. Therefore t_{i(k)} → 0, c_{i(k)} → b and s_{k+k₀} → 0. It follows that t′_k = t_{i(k)}·s_{k+k₀} → 0·0 = 0 (Tendsto.mul) and c′_k = c_{i(k)} + t_{i(k)}•y → b + 0•y = b (Tendsto.add, Tendsto.smul_const).
6. (Weak convergence.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) be a test form. By step 1, currentEval(blowUp T (c_{φ(k)} + t_{φ(k)}•y) (t_{φ(k)}s_k)) ω → C(ω). Composing this real sequence with k ↦ k + k₀ (which tends to ∞) gives a sequence with the same limit, and its k-th term is currentEval(blowUp T c′_k t′_k) ω: the centres and scales agree, and the proofs of nonvanishing of the scale inside blowUp are irrelevant (proof irrelevance). Hence currentEval(blowUp T c′_k t′_k) ω → C(ω) for every ω, i.e. blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C.
Steps 3–6 show that (c′_k), (t′_k) satisfy all requirements: t′_k > 0, dist(c′_k, z) < r − t′_k, t′_k → 0, c′_k → b and blowUp T c′_k t′_k ⇀ C. ∎

Choose k₀ with s_k < 1 − ‖y‖ for all k ≥ k₀ (s_k → 0 and ‖y‖ < 1).
Put c′_k := c_{φ(k+k₀)} + t_{φ(k+k₀)}y and t′_k := t_{φ(k+k₀)}s_{k+k₀} > 0; the triangle inequality gives dist(c′_k, z) < r − t_{φ(k+k₀)}(1 − ‖y‖) < r − t′_k.
t′_k → 0 and c′_k → b, and the tail k ↦ k + k₀ of the weakly convergent sequence of step 1 converges weakly to C.
